oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Introduction to Hans-Georg Gadamer’s“Hermeneutics and Theology”: Gadamer on Theology as a Human Science
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: DeHoust, Brady
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: Gadamer
hermeneneutics
theology
human science
faith
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: “Hermeneutics and Theology,” addressed to theologians, represents Gadamer’s account of the task of theology considered as a human science. In this brief translator's introduction, I will first relate the original context of Gadamer's 1977 essay. I will then proceed to summarize the essay, focusing on aspects distinct from Gadamer’s other writings on theology and religion. These include Gadamer’s distinction between religious discourses, his analysis of theology as a “secondary form of reflection” vis a vis faith, and his explication of theology in terms of hermeneutics and Aristotelian practical philosophy. Finally, I will indicate some relevant areas of scholarship to which this new translation ought to be relevant, including Gadamerian approaches to theology and religious studies, contemporary debates in the philosophy of revelation, and broader ethical and political applications of Gadamerian thought.
oai_dc:dc.dc:source: Journal of Gadamer Studies; Vol. 1 No. 2 (2026): Language, Virtue, Friendship and Communal Practice
